subject: Information Theory
title: GDPR and Information Rights
description: A 60-second lesson on GDPR and Information Rights.

hook.text: The EU's GDPR fined Meta $1.3 billion in 2023 for transferring user data. Privacy became legally enforceable.

buildup.text: GDPR grants data subjects rights: access, deletion, portability, and the right to know how their data is processed.

discovery.text: The regulation treats personal data as belonging to the individual. Companies are custodians, not owners.

twist.text: Enforcement is uneven. Small companies struggle with compliance costs while tech giants absorb fines as business costs.

climax.text: GDPR inspired similar laws worldwide. The information rights movement is reshaping the global data economy.

punchline.text: Your data, your rights. Regulation catches up to technology.

quiz.question: What fundamental principle does GDPR establish about personal data?
options: Companies own all data they collect
Personal data belongs to the individual, not the collector
